**RA Progress Statement — Seoul–Daegu Honorific Shift Corpus**  
Reporting date: November 9, 2026  
Prepared by: [Your name]

This statement documents my annotation progress and the timeline affecting the fall-term target for the Seoul–Daegu honorific shift corpus. The fall target was 6,000 utterances annotated. As of November 9, I have completed 4,200, or 70% of the target. I am the only RA doing Korean annotation on the project.

The six-week schedule delay was caused by the IRB amendment needed to add the 14 new Daegu recordings remaining unsigned until October 15, 2026. I sent the amendment to Prof. Hollander for signature on September 3 and sent reminders on September 12, September 24, and October 6; I have copies of all three. I was not permitted to begin annotating the new recordings until the amendment was signed. The interval from September 3 to October 15 is the six-week period described at the November 6 lab meeting as “six weeks behind.”

During that waiting period, I completed work that was not in the original timeline: I recoded 2,300 existing utterances using the revised speech-level scheme Prof. Hollander requested in August. Since October 15, I have annotated approximately 1,900 utterances, averaging over 500 per week. The original plan assumed 350 per week. At the current pace, I expect to reach 6,000 utterances by the end of January 2027.

For the Winter 2027 funding review, I ask that the record reflect the IRB signature delay as the cause of the six-week gap and count the recoding of 2,300 utterances during that period as progress. If the review cannot include that context, I ask that the “six weeks behind” comment not be included.
